title: Best Salary Packaging Australia: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay using a 38-hour week, 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and best salary packaging Australia tips.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, use hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. Remember that super is paid on top of this amount.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the base minimum set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries or occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Your actual pay may be higher than the minimum if your award or agreement says so.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, intended to compensate for lack of paid leave. If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate is typically the base rate plus 25%. For example, the National Minimum Wage casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate in the formula, but remember that casuals do not accrue annual or sick leave.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you are paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your finances. The standard formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This article explains how to apply it, what assumptions to make, and how tax, super, and the **best salary packaging australia** options fit in.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

Most full-time roles in Australia are based on a 38-hour week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. When you use our [the timesheet](/) tool, you can enter any weekly hours, but for a typical full-time conversion we assume 38 hours. If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. The formula remains the same: multiply your hourly rate by your actual weekly hours, then by 52.

### From Hourly to Fortnightly

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, your weekly gross is $1,140, and your fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can be useful for budgeting and comparing with salary offers that are quoted per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. Always check your award rate rather than relying solely on the national minimum. If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that gives $33.05 per hour. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer must contribute an additional $7,200 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer. When negotiating a salary, remember that the total employment cost includes super. The **best salary packaging australia** strategies can help you use your pre-tax salary for certain benefits, but super is separate.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. You also pay the Medicare levy, generally 2% of your taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you estimate your net income after tax and Medicare. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles are based on 2025–26 figures in our calculator, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate.

### Using the Formula: Examples

Let’s say you earn $35 per hour and work 38 hours a week. Your annual gross is $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. Your fortnightly gross is $35 × 38 × 2 = $2,660. After tax (using the 2026–27 rates) and Medicare, your take-home pay would be lower. If you are a casual at $35 base plus 25% loading, your hourly rate becomes $43.75, and annual gross becomes $86,450. Remember that casuals do not receive paid leave, so the higher hourly rate compensates for that.

### Average Weekly Earnings and Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages across all industries and occupations, not medians for a specific job. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context. Do not confuse an industry average with the median pay for your role; use [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources for more targeted information.

### Salary Packaging and the Best Options

Salary packaging (also called salary sacrifice) allows you to use pre-tax income for certain expenses like a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. The **best salary packaging australia** arrangements can reduce your taxable income and increase your take-home pay, but they are not included in our basic conversion calculator. For example, packaging a car through a novated lease can save tax if structured correctly. Always consult a professional or use the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to understand the rules. Our calculator assumes no salary sacrifice, so your actual tax may differ if you package benefits.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Further Reading

For more detailed conversion tools, visit our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page. If you need to check award rates, see the [pay guides](/blog). And remember, the [reference tables](/data) on our site provide up-to-date figures from Fair Work and the ATO.
